ei.title: 3번: The Timeless Trap of Shopping Malls
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making impulsive purchases.

questions.passage: If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it (A)[difficult / easy] to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become (B)[exhausted / energized] from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making (C)[rational / impulsive] purchases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) difficult=어려운 / easy=쉬운 (B) exhausted=지친 / energized=활력 넘치는 (C) impulsive=충동적인 / rational=이성적인
det.analysis:
① easy: 게임 환경은 시간 파악을 '어렵게' 만든다 → difficult
② difficult—exhausted—impulsive: 시간 파악이 어렵고, 뇌가 지치며, 충동 구매로 이어짐 ←정답
③ energized/rational: 결정을 많이 해 '지치고' '충동적'이 됨. 반대
④ 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 게임/쇼핑몰이 시간 인식을 흐트러뜨림 → difficult, exhausted, impulsive의 부정적 흐름

It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more (A)[susceptible / resistant] to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then (B)[enjoy / regret] the purchase later. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) susceptible=취약한 / resistant=저항하는 (B) regret=후회하다 / enjoy=즐기다 (C) overwhelm=압도하다 / relax=편안하게 하다
det.analysis:
① resistant: 잘못된 판단에 '취약해짐' → susceptible
② enjoy/relax: 나쁜 구매를 '후회'하고, 몰은 '압도'하려 설계됨. 반대
③ susceptible—regret—overwhelm: 취약해지고, 후회하며, 압도당함 ←정답
④ resistant/enjoy: 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 나쁜 판단에 취약(susceptible) → 후회(regret) → 몰이 우리를 압도(overwhelm)하는 부정적 흐름

It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to (B)[poor / wise] decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are (C)[carelessly / cleverly] designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making impulsive purchases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) create=만들어내다 / prevent=막다 (B) poor=형편없는 / wise=현명한 (C) cleverly=교묘하게 / carelessly=부주의하게
det.analysis:
① create—poor—cleverly: 몰은 시간 인식 변화를 '만들어내고', 우리는 '형편없는' 판단을 하며, 몰은 '교묘하게' 설계됨 ←정답
② prevent: 몰은 변화를 '막는' 게 아니라 만들어냄. 반대
③ wise/carelessly: 판단은 형편없고, 설계는 교묘함. 반대
④ 모두 반대
det.tip: 몰은 의도적으로(create, cleverly) 우리를 형편없는(poor) 판단으로 유도

det.korean: ① perception=인식 ② phenomenon=현상 ③ difficult→easy (부적절) ④ exhausted=지친

④ (A) 세다 (B) 구별하다: (A) 진실을 세다? 부적절

① perception: 인식 — 슬픔·실망의 감정이 아님
② regret: 후회 — 한 일이나 하지 못한 일에 대한 슬픔·실망의 감정 ←정답
③ phenomenon: 현상 — 감정이 아님
④ purchase: 구매 — 감정이 아님
det.tip: sadness or disappointment about something you have done = 후회(regret)

questions.passage: We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become __________ (exhaust) from making too many decisions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: exhaust(동사: 지치게 하다) → exhausted(과거분사: 지친). become + p.p. 형태로 상태를 나타냄
det.analysis: exhaust를 과거분사 exhausted로 변환. 'become exhausted'=지치게 되다. 사람·뇌가 '지쳐지는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 필요
det.tip: become + 형용사/과거분사. 뇌가 '지친' 상태 → exhausted

questions.passage: This happens because malls are cleverly __________ (design) to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making impulsive purchases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: design(동사: 설계하다) → designed(과거분사). 'be + p.p.' 수동태 (몰이 '설계되다')
det.analysis: design을 과거분사 designed로 변환. 'malls are designed'=몰이 '설계된다' — 몰은 설계하는 주체가 아니라 설계되는 대상이므로 be+p.p. 수동태
det.tip: are + _____ → 수동태(be + p.p.) → designed. 몰이 '설계됨'

questions.passage: If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to __________, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making impulsive purchases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: more time shopping=더 많은 쇼핑 시간 / too many decisions=너무 많은 결정 / temporal distortion=시간 왜곡 / poor decision-making=형편없는 의사결정
det.analysis:
① more time shopping: 쇼핑 시간에 '취약'? 어색
② too many decisions: 결정을 많이 하는 것은 원인이지 취약해지는 대상이 아님
③ temporal distortion: 시간 왜곡 → 앞부분 개념, 이 자리와 연결 안 됨
④ poor decision-making: 지친 뇌가 '형편없는 의사결정'에 취약해져 나쁜 구매를 함 ←정답
det.tip: more susceptible to _____, causing bad purchases → poor decision-making(형편없는 판단)

questions.passage: If you've ever been inside a shopping mall, you probably noticed that there were no clocks or windows. The reason for this is to create a change in our perception of time, also known as a "temporal distortion." You have likely experienced this phenomenon while playing video games. It felt like you were playing for minutes, but it was actually hours. This is because the gaming environment makes it difficult to tell how much time has passed. The same thing happens in malls. We end up spending more time shopping, which leads the brain to become exhausted from making too many decisions. This leaves us more susceptible to poor decision-making, causing us to make bad purchases. For instance, we might end up buying stuff we don't actually want or need and then regret the purchase later. This happens because malls are cleverly designed to overwhelm us, pushing us toward making __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: temporal distortion=시간 왜곡 / poor decision-making=형편없는 의사결정 / too many decisions=너무 많은 결정 / impulsive purchases=충동 구매
det.analysis:
① temporal distortion: 시간 왜곡을 '만들도록' 몰아감? 앞부분 개념
② poor decision-making: 형편없는 판단은 원인이지 몰이 밀어붙이는 '구매' 자체가 아님
③ too many decisions: 결정을 많이 하는 것은 앞 문장의 원인
④ impulsive purchases: 몰이 우리를 압도해 '충동 구매'로 몰아감 ←정답
det.tip: overwhelm us, pushing us toward making _____ → impulsive purchases(충동 구매)
